title: Cartesian projection formula for extension from a coefficient vertex
statement: Let J, B and τ be the site and ring-sheaf tower of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], with independent site universes c,v and coefficient universe max(c,v,r). Fix the scalar data, closed tensor structures, K-flat tensor models, tensorEvaluation comparisons and their ordinaryEvaluationTensor normalization of [def-coef-semilinear-derived-calculus]. For a cartesian derived system M and a vertex n, let L be any left adjoint of the actual derived evaluation e_n, with adjunction adj. For every P in D(B_n), the inverse adjunction transpose of (η_P tensor 1) followed by tensorEvaluation_n inverse is an isomorphism L(P tensor M_n) → L(P) tensor M. This is a tensor projection formula only: it neither supplies a left adjoint nor asserts an internal-Hom comparison.

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p.21; Proposition 4.17(a) and its proof, printed pp.25-26. The unit-defined projection argument is step 2 of lem-coef-semilinear-cartesian-hom-evaluation; the extension from constant quotient rings to arbitrary sheaves of commutative rings is the same local tensor computation.

proof.text: Prove joint detection for the actual sequence-site evaluations. Transport to strict systems by strictSystemSequenceEquivalence and its derived equivalence. The evaluation comparison is pushforwardCongr for the identity structural ring maps, derived by mapDerivedCategoryCompIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso. Apply systemDerivedEvaluation_isIso_iff and reflection by the equivalence.

For q at most n, apply semilinearProjectionBelowFactorization to the actual specified adjunction and scalar(h). Normalized M makes reduction(h) invertible. The product of this reduction with the identity is an isomorphism, so its tensor image is invertible. The factorization makes e_q(f) followed by tensorEvaluation_q invertible; cancel that comparison.

For q greater than n, compare the given L and its adjunction to derived singleton extension composed with the derived strict-system/sequence-site equivalence. Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq and the evaluation comparison transport systemSingleDerivedAbove to e_q L for every input. This gives zero for the source of e_q(f) and for e_q(LP). The closed tensorRight is a left adjoint and hence preserves zero. TensorEvaluation_q transports this zero to the target of e_q(f). Every map between zero objects is invertible. Apply joint evaluation detection to f.

proof_origin.place: Construction 4.1, printed p.21; Proposition 4.17(a), printed pp.25-26. Lean proof by below-level factorization, proved upper-level vanishing, and proved transport of joint evaluation detection.

mathlib_searches.query: Projection formula for a left adjoint implies its right adjoint commutes with internal Hom in a cartesian first variable

mathlib_searches.results: Found proved SystemSingleDerivedExtension, SystemSingleDerivedEvaluation, SystemRingedSequenceSite, SystemEvaluationTopos. Their adjunction supplies the parent left adjoint. UnitAdjunctTensorAction proves coherence, without invertibility. ClosedScalarHomComparison treats a tensor-preserving left adjoint, and does not supply the cartesian projection map for a right evaluation functor. No duplicate of this projection statement found.

from.place: Step 2 of lem-coef-semilinear-cartesian-hom-evaluation: projection for extension from a vertex, before applying the tensor-Hom adjunctions.

lean.statement:
theorem semilinearCartesianProjection
    (scalar : ∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m),
      ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r} (coefficientMap.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ h))
    (closed : Closed.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
      (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ))
    (models : Models.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
      (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) closed)
    (level : ∀ n : ℕ, Closed.{c, v, r} J (B n))
    (levelModels : ∀ n : ℕ, Models.{c, v, r} J (B n) (level n))
    (tensorEvaluation : ∀ n : ℕ,
      closed.tensor ⋙ e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n ≅
        ((e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).prod
          (e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n)) ⋙ (level n).tensor)
    (tensorModel : ∀ n : ℕ,
      TensorComparisonModel.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J) J
        (systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) (B n)
        (evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n) closed (level n) models
        (levelModels n) (tensorEvaluation n))
    (ordinary : ∀ (n : ℕ) (M N : Systems.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ),
      (tensorModel n).ordinary M N = ordinaryEvaluationTensor.{c, v, r} J B τ n M N)
    (M : DS.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ)
    (hM : Normalized.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ scalar M) (n : ℕ) :
    ∀ (L : D.{c, v, max c v r} J (B n) ⥤ DS.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ)
      (adj : L ⊣ e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n)
      (P : D.{c, v, max c v r} J (B n)),
      IsIso ((adj.homEquiv _ _).symm
        ((level n).tensor.map
            (Prod.mkHom (adj.unit.app P)
              (𝟙 ((e.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).obj M))) ≫
          (tensorEvaluation n).inv.app (L.obj P, M)))
